title: Preparation of 10% Triton X-100 Solution
author: Allen Institute for Brain Science
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bezhjf36
materials: 10% Triton X-100 stock solution for use in IHC reagents.

Triton X-100, when added to aqueous solutions acts as a surfactant, decreasing the surface tension of the solution. It also punches holes in membranes, allowing easier penetration of macrmolecules into cells and organelles, and reduces non-specific binding of antisera in immunohistochemistry.

steps.title: Gather RNase‑free equipment
steps.instruction: Obtain an RNase‑free 1 L container and an RNase‑free magnetic stir bar.

steps.title: Add MilliQ water
steps.instruction: Using a graduated cylinder, measure 900 mL of MilliQ water into the RNase‑free 1 L bottle that already contains the stir bar.

steps.title: Add Triton X‑100
steps.instruction: Add 100 mL of Triton X‑100 to the bottle containing the 900 mL of MilliQ water.

steps.title: Mix solution
steps.instruction: Stir the mixture on a magnetic stir plate set to 5 or higher for about 15 minutes, or until the Triton X‑100 is fully dissolved.

steps.title: Remove stir bar and label
steps.instruction: Remove the stir bar with a magnetic stir bar remover, wrap the bottle in foil, and label it with the reagent name, preparation date, and preparer’s initials.

steps.title: Store solution
steps.instruction: Keep the foil‑wrapped bottle protected from light and store it at room temperature; the 10 % Triton X‑100 solution is stable for up to 12 weeks.

steps.title: Dispose of empty container
steps.instruction: Place the empty container in a plastic recycling bin.

steps.title: Dispose of Triton solution
steps.instruction: The 10 % Triton X‑100 solution may be poured down any sink and into the municipal sewer system.
